cards.example:
- Don’t hang up yet — I still need your delivery address.
Não desligue ainda — eu ainda preciso do seu endereço de entrega.
cards.note: Hang up on someone = desligar na cara de alguém.

cards.definition: To phone someone again, or to return their call.
cards.example:
- I’m walking into a meeting; can I call you back in twenty minutes?
Estou entrando numa reunião; posso te retornar em vinte minutos?
cards.note: Separável: call you back. Substantivo: a callback.

cards.definition: With the microphone turned off, so nobody can hear you.
cards.example:
- You are on mute, Marcos — we can see you, but we can’t hear you.
Você está no mudo, Marcos — a gente te vê, mas não te ouve.
cards.note: On mute / unmute yourself — o clássico das videochamadas.

cards.definition: A service that records a message when you cannot answer.
cards.example:
- If I don’t answer, leave a message on my voicemail and I’ll return it.
Se eu não atender, deixe recado na minha caixa postal que eu retorno.
cards.note: Leave a voicemail; “caiu na caixa postal” = it went to voicemail.

cards.example:
- Could you speak up a little? The audio is very low on my side.
Pode falar um pouco mais alto? O áudio está muito baixo aqui.
cards.note: Também significa “se posicionar”: speak up in meetings.

cards.definition: To press the numbers to make a phone call.
cards.example:
- Dial 9 first to get an outside line from the office phones.
Disque 9 primeiro para conseguir linha externa nos telefones do escritório.
cards.note: Dial in = entrar numa chamada; dial the wrong number = discar errado.

cards.definition: To make a caller wait on the line.
cards.example:
- The attendant put me on hold for ten minutes with that terrible music.
O atendente me deixou na espera por dez minutos com aquela musiquinha horrível.
cards.note: Separável: put you on hold. “Estou na espera” = I’m on hold.

cards.definition: Said when the signal is bad and the voice is cutting out.
cards.example:
- Sorry, you’re breaking up — can you repeat the last part?
Desculpe, está cortando — pode repetir a última parte?
cards.note: Nada a ver com términos de namoro aqui: é o áudio falhando.

cards.definition: An agreement where each side gives up something.
cards.example:
- After two hours of negotiation, we finally reached a compromise on the price.
Depois de duas horas de negociação, finalmente chegamos a um meio-termo no preço.

cards.definition: A talk to an audience; also a long telling-off.
cards.example:
- The manager gave us a lecture about arriving late to client calls.
O gerente nos deu um sermão sobre chegar atrasado às calls com clientes.
cards.note: “Leitura” é reading. Give someone a lecture = passar um sermão.

questions.prompt: She ended the call while you were still speaking. She…
questions.explanation: “Hang up ON someone” is the rude one. The past is “hung”.

questions.prompt: I'm walking into a meeting; can I _____ you in twenty minutes?
questions.explanation: With a pronoun it splits: “call you back”, never “call back you”.

questions.prompt: You are on _____, Marcos — we can see you but we can't hear you.
If I don't answer, leave a message on my _____.
questions.explanation: You LEAVE a message — the Portuguese “deixar” tempts “let”.

questions.prompt: Você pode falar mais alto? O áudio está muito baixo.
questions.answer: Could you speak up? The audio is very low.|Can you speak up? The audio is very low.
questions.explanation: “Speak up” is to raise your voice; “speak out” is to state an opinion publicly.

questions.prompt: _____ 9 first to get an outside line.
questions.explanation: “Dial” a number; the noun “dial tone” comes from the same word.

questions.prompt: The attendant made you wait on the line for ten minutes. She…
questions.explanation: The person goes in the middle: put me / him / the client on hold.

questions.prompt: Sorry, _____ — can you repeat the last part?
questions.explanation: Said about a bad signal, not about a relationship.

questions.prompt: After two hours, both sides gave up something and agreed. They reached a…
questions.explanation: “Compromise” is the middle ground. The Portuguese “compromisso” is “appointment” or “commitment”.

questions.prompt: The manager talked to the team for ten minutes about arriving late. He gave them a…
questions.explanation: “Lecture” is a talk or a telling-off. The Portuguese “leitura” is “reading”.
